statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of French language and Latin alphabet; no transliteration required beyond standard French conventions
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical to existing companies without consent
Words implying public service or regulated activity without prior authorization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and incorporation services

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce): Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée - SAS); Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general company law); Articles R.123-30 to R.123-80 (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS); single-business filing window (Guichet Unique) implementing rules under Order No. 2021-300 of 19 March 2021.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) acting through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) Guichet Unique online portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution de société (Company Formation Declaration) filed electronically on the Guichet Unique, accompanied by the signed Statuts (Articles of Association), the attestation de dépôt de fonds and the attestation de parution (legal publication certificate).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS (Article L.227-2). Where the Articles fix a capital, at least 50% of the nominal value of cash subscriptions must be paid up at incorporation and held in a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) at a licensed bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; funds are released only upon production of the Kbis registration extract. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up and, unless the statutory de minimis exemption applies, certified by a commissaire aux apports (Article L.225-8, R.225-7).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF [SAS NAME]
Resolved unanimously:
1. That the draft Articles of Association be and hereby are adopted as the governing statute of the company.
2. That the subscribed share capital of €[X], fully subscribed, with at least 50% of cash contributions paid into a blocked escrow account, be approved; the president is authorized to release funds upon registration.
3. That the registered office is fixed at [address], France.
4. That [Name] is appointed President, with powers to act on behalf of the company.
5. That the President be authorized to complete all filings with the Guichet Unique and to open the company bank account.
Adopted unanimously. [Signature, Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Verification, Registered Office Domiciliation and Execution of Statuts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI data portal (data.inpi.fr) for name availability and trademark pre-search; external counsel for drafting; no notarial deed required unless a real-property contribution or specific legal formalities apply.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the availability of the corporate name and confirm compatibility of the corporate purpose with UN38.3 battery testing and CE-RED electromagnetic laboratory activities. Secure the registered office by lease, ownership or approved domiciliation company (for a maximum of five years). Draft the Statuts in French, record the SAS corporate object, capital, share classes, governance of the Président, and execute by all shareholders by wet-ink signature or qualified electronic signature under the rules of the 28 September 2020 order. Non-signing shareholders must act through a formal power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Name availability and trademark search result
Draft Articles of Association (Statuts) in French language
Power of attorney for any represented shareholder
Rapport du commissaire aux apports where in-kind contributions exceed the exemption threshold
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar queries the corporate object or capital provisions, the shareholders may adopt a corrective unanimous written resolution under Article L.227-9 and resubmit the amended Statuts within the statutory curing period without re-paying the main filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Escrow Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed in France or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional 'compte bloqué' in the name of the company under formation. Pay at least 50% of the nominal value of cash subscriptions by each subscriber. The bank issues an attestation de dépôt des fonds stating the amount held and the bank's irrevocable undertaking to block the funds until the Kbis is produced and to release them only on presentment of the Kbis extract and the company's definitive bank details.
required_dossiers: Original or certified electronic copies of the signed Statuts
Identity document of the president and of each cash contributor
Bank KYC, AML and sanctions-compliance questionnaire
Proof of execution of the contribution payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of refusal of registration, the funds remain blocked and are restituted pro rata to each subscriber upon written request, in accordance with the refund procedure of Article R.225-10-2; the attestation may be re-issued by the bank for a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Statutory Legal Notice (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A journal d'annonces légales (JAL) approved in the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place a constitution notice in the authorized JAL within one month of signature of the Statuts. The notice shall state the corporate name, form (SAS), registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, number and type of shares, president's name and the RCS registry where the company will be filed, per Articles R.210-1 to R.210-3. Obtain the attestation de parution evidencing the date and venue of publication.
required_dossiers: Legal notice draft (capsule) containing the statutory particulars
Signed Statuts for the JAL editor's verification
Payment receipt of the publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected or contains a factual error, publish a corrective notice in the same JAL; the date of the initial valid publication remains the reference for the short limitation period of third-party claims under Article R.210-5.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Formation Declaration with the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; the file is routed to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS registration and automatically to INSEE, URSSAF and DGFiP.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Déclaration de constitution de société using the graphical subscription certificate; attach the signed Statuts, attestation de dépôt des fonds, attestation de parution, proof of registered-office rights and identity/consent of the president. Pay the statutory filing fee of EUR 37.44 (approximately USD 41), which excludes legal-publication cost. Submit once all checks pass; the greffe performs legal review and registers the company in the RCS.
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt des fonds (escrow capital certificate)
Attestation de parution from the legal announcement journal
Proof of registered-office rights (lease or domiciliation certificate)
Consent of the president to hold office
Identity copies of the president and, where applicable, of represented shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The guichet unique must notify any missing document; the filer has 15 days to supplement the file. If the greffe rejects the declaration, correct the dossier and re-submit within the allowed delay; a final refusal may be challenged before the presiding judge of the Commercial Court in interim proceedings (référé) within one month.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) for non-established businesses; official portal: impots.gouv.fr. Company formation and statutory business registration are completed through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with SIREN/SIRET allocation by INSEE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the SAS through the INPI Guichet unique and obtain its registration extract, SIREN and SIRET numbers. 2. File the required tax registration information with the competent SIE through the business creation process and provide the articles of association, registration extract, registered-office evidence, directors' details, business activity description, bank details and expected taxable transactions. 3. The DGFiP issues the French corporate tax account identifiers and, where applicable, the intracommunity VAT identification number in the format FR plus a two-digit key and the SIREN. 4. A foreign entity without a French establishment applies to the SIEE for French VAT registration when it makes taxable supplies in France that are not fully subject to the domestic reverse charge or another exemption. The application generally requires proof of foreign incorporation, foreign tax identification, certificate of tax residence, constitutional documents, identity and authority documents for the representative, description of French activities, contracts or invoices, and banking information. 5. EU-established applicants may generally use the applicable electronic or administrative channel of their home tax authority; non-EU entities may need a French fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement or statutory exception removes that requirement. 6. Validate the VAT number through the European Commission VIES system where relevant. VAT registration does not by itself replace customs EORI registration, which is required for customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). An eligible SAS may elect temporarily for income-tax treatment under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code, generally for a maximum period of five financial years, provided statutory conditions are met, including limits relating to headcount, turnover or balance-sheet total, age of the company, ownership and management. The election is not a general check-the-box regime and must be exercised within the statutory time limit. An SAS may not generally elect the partnership-style permanent pass-through treatment available to certain other French entities. France has implemented anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework; these are anti-avoidance provisions, not a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA), based on the EU VAT Directive and French VAT legislation in the French Tax Code.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the French VAT franchise regime, the principal turnover threshold for supplies of services is EUR 37,500, with a tolerance threshold generally of EUR 41,250, subject to the applicable tax year and statutory updates. Different thresholds apply to supplies of goods and certain regulated activities. Exceeding the relevant threshold or making taxable transactions outside the franchise regime can require immediate VAT registration. The threshold does not eliminate registration obligations arising from specific cross-border, import, export, distance-selling, or taxable-establishment rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting in phases. From 1 September 2026, all French-established businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices; issuance obligations initially apply to large companies and in-scope intermediate-sized companies, followed generally by small and medium-sized businesses from 1 September 2027. Domestic business-to-business invoices will be transmitted through the public invoicing portal or an approved private Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP). Cross-border and certain business-to-consumer transactions are generally subject to electronic transaction reporting rather than domestic invoice transmission. France does not operate a universal real-time pre-clearance model for all invoices. Invoices must contain legally required identification, VAT, payment, date, numbering and transaction information, and must be retained in an auditable electronic format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to a destination outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT with the right to deduct input VAT where the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU by the seller or by an authorized intermediary and the exporter can substantiate the export and exit from the EU customs territory. The seller must preserve the customs export declaration and reliable evidence of exit. Intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-identified customer in another EU Member State may be exempt with the right to deduct input VAT if the customer has a valid VAT number, the goods are transported to another Member State, the supplier retains transport evidence, and the required recapitulative statement and reporting are completed. For laboratory testing and certification services, a B2B service supplied to a business customer established outside France is generally outside the scope of French VAT under the place-of-supply rule, rather than a French zero-rated export. B2B services supplied to an EU or non-EU business customer generally follow the customer's establishment and may require reverse-charge wording. Special rules apply to services connected with movable tangible property, B2C customers, and services effectively used or enjoyed in France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration containing the applicable customs procedure and Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit certification or equivalent electronic evidence that the goods physically exited the European Union
Commercial invoice, sales contract, packing list and transport documentation
Bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note or other carrier evidence, as applicable
Proof of transport and delivery to the non-EU destination
Exporter, declarant and customs representative records, including EORI details
For intra-Community supplies: customer VAT identification number, transport evidence and recapitulative statement

For offshore B2B services: customer legal identity, foreign business or VAT identification, contract, service report, place-of-supply analysis and invoice containing the applicable reverse-charge or outside-scope wording
Payment records and accounting records supporting the transaction; France does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a condition for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for establishing export VAT exemption or service place of supply. Export evidence must nevertheless be complete, consistent and retained for the applicable statutory audit period. If zero-rating or exemption is denied, unpaid French VAT may be assessed retrospectively, together with late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month and tax penalties. A 40% penalty may apply for deliberate failure or deliberate inaccuracies, and an 80% penalty may apply in cases involving fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law, subject to statutory conditions. False, incomplete or manipulated customs declarations may trigger customs duties, VAT, customs penalties and other sanctions. Serious fraudulent conduct may create criminal tax-fraud exposure. Input VAT refunds can be reduced, denied or clawed back where export, transport, customer-status, invoicing or accounting substantiation is inadequate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a fully convertible currency regime for both current and capital accounts in full compliance with EU and IMF standards. Capital account transactions, including profit remittances to non-resident shareholders, are unrestricted subject to standard tax clearance, beneficial ownership verification, and anti-money laundering documentation. No capital controls or convertibility hurdles apply to established EU-based entities conducting cross-border trade or laboratory services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: French exporters must declare all export receipts to customs authorities for statistical purposes. Repatriation of foreign currency proceeds is strongly recommended within six months of shipment or per contractual terms. Authorized banks facilitate conversion to EUR at the official rate; non-repatriation may trigger enhanced reporting to the Banque de France and potential tax penalties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for cross-border electronic money transfers via regulated platforms such as Wise or Revolut Business, subject to full AML/KYC compliance, local regulatory approvals, and restrictions on offshore digital wallet operations for French entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding with video KYC is permitted for low-risk corporate clients under French banking regulations. Physical presence or director video interview is mandatory for accounts handling transactions above €50,000 or involving high-risk activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned jurisdictions, politically exposed persons, or adverse media screening hits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of funds statement, beneficial ownership certificate, PEP declaration, and independent due diligence report

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction patterns or unexplained large inbound wires
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade contracts, invoices, laboratory service agreements, and bank reference letters to substantiate commercial purpose

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections processed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 100 (Capital), supported by source-of-funds documentation, beneficial ownership verification, and tax clearance certificates to satisfy Banque de France and French banking AML requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements routed through SWIFT MT103 or MT202; Commercial Letters of Credit available via Banque de France-approved correspondent banks for international laboratory equipment or service payments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements filing (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via INPI/Infogreffe (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual shareholders' meeting must approve financial accounts within 6 months of fiscal year end; filing with the RCS must occur within 1 month of approval, or within 6 months of fiscal year end if no extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers administrative injunction and penalty of up to EUR 1,500 (individual) / EUR 15,000 (legal representative); continued non-filing exposes the entity to RCS strike-off proceedings and a separate ’non-dépôt’ penalty of EUR 500 per month from the identity verification service.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal years ending 31 December: online filing by 3 May (tax declaration) and 15 May (financial schedule); for off-calendar fiscal years, within 3 months of year-end plus a 15-day extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes a 5% late-payment penalty (plus 0.2% monthly interest) and a surcharge of 10% if not filed within 30 days of formal notice; persistent failure triggers tax lien and an automatic 5% increase on the assessed tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT declaration (CA12, CA3 or CACF aggregated)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly CA3 declaration due by the 15th of the following month; annual CA12 declaration by the 20th of the second month after year-end (or 30 June for calendar-year taxpayers under the annual settlement scheme)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers an interest charge of 0.2% per month and a penalty of 5% on the unpaid amount, plus a possible EUR 750 fine for late annual declaration; repeated failure may expose the company to a 25% penalty for deliberate concealment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CVAE declaration and payment (if turnover exceeds EUR 500,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration on form 1330-CVAE and payment via the online TVA module by 3 May (for calendar-year taxpayers); provisional instalments due 15 June and 15 September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid CVAE accrues 0.2% monthly interest plus a 5% late-payment penalty; failure to file the annual declaration may trigger a EUR 750 fine and a recalculated assessment based on administrative estimates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation record (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) via the Guichet Unique (INPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing required within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; an annual confirmation protocol must be documented at the fiscal year-end and submitted immediately if a change occurs during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to disclose or updating late exposes the legal representative to up to EUR 90,000 in fines and 6 months’ imprisonment; the entity may also be ordered to regularize the declaration by the Grenoble registry under a RCS disciplinary procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate record audit and register verification (procès-verbal d’assemblée générale and minutes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory records held at registered office; no filing fee are payable unless the minutes are filed with the RCS for certain corporate acts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must be convened no later than 6 months after fiscal year-end; signed minutes must be bound in the minute book and maintained with the register of members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or untimely shareholder approval renders the accounts s non-opposable to third parties but does not carry a civil penalty; failure to keep prescribed registers is an administrative offence punishable by EUR 360 fine, and may trigger an RCS audit or strike-off request.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Société par Actions Simplifiée is legally required to appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the fiscal year-end: (i) net turnover of EUR 8,000,000, (ii) total balance sheet assets of EUR 4,000,000, or (iii) an average workforce of 50 employees. Mandatory appointment is also required if the company controls or is controlled by entities meeting these thresholds, or if the company operates in a sector subject to specific legal audit requirements. For battery-safety testing under ISIC 7120, a stronger grace period is not applicable; compulsory audit applies from the first exercise exceeding the thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French statutory accounts must be prepared in accordance with the Plan Comptable Général (PCG) under the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), transposing Directive 2013/34/EU. Listed groups are required to use EU-adopted IFRS for consolidated accounts; unconsolidated SAS accounts remain under French GAAP (PCG). The PCG requires the true-and-fair view principle, detailed notes, and the use of the fixed-balance sheet format.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative must verify and update the beneficial ownership register at least once every fiscal year, regardless of whether a material change occurred. Share transfers must be recorded in the register of members within the timeframe specified by the SAS’s statutory provisions and the RBE declaration must be formally refiled within 30 days of any transfer affecting UBO status. The annual confirmation must be prepared at the fiscal year-end, dated, and signed by the president (président) or a delegate authorized by the board, and retained in the corporate minute book.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des mouvements de titres and registre des associés)
Register of Directors (Registre des décisions du président and minutes of general meetings)
Minute Book (registre de procès-verbaux des assemblées générales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 – USD 1,800 per annum for a commercial registered-office address in France (Paris / regional hub rates)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 25,000 per annum for a certified audit firm (commissaire aux comptes) covering statutory control, sampling, and sign-off under PCG for a small to mid-sized SAS testing laboratory

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credits (up to 5% of qualifying R&D expenses), innovation status benefits, accelerated depreciation allowances, and temporary tax exemptions in designated zones

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 - Déclaration de résultat via impots.gouv.fr electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the 4th month following fiscal year-end (e.g., 15 April for calendar year FYE 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only French-source income; foreign income generally exempt

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for operating expenses, interest, and provisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Limited to French-source expenses; TP adjustments apply
Corporate tax base; losses carried forward

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 0.5% per month of tax due (minimum 125 EUR), maximum 5% or 75,000 EUR; non-payment interest at 0.2% per month

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Apply for TRC (Traitement de la Réduction de la Source) via impots.gouv.fr with DTA certificate and beneficial ownership proof; relief often results in 0% or 5% rate for qualifying EU/ treaty partners
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% to 10% (treaty-dependent, e.g., 0% for many OECD countries); Interest: 12.8% statutory, reduced to 0% under most treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 50,000,000 EUR (annual turnover threshold triggering Master File and Local File requirements)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France adheres to OECD BEPS Action 5; economic substance requirements apply to entities claiming treaty benefits or holding IP, with annual substance reporting obligations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction with up to 5 years imprisonment and fines equal to 80% of evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors face personal criminal liability, restitution orders, and possible imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to apply arm's length principle or maintain inadequate documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment of profits, penalties of 80% of additional tax due, and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal joint and several liability for tax adjustments; potential civil claims and reputational damage

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing French entity without genuine business operations or substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 10% of turnover, potential dissolution, and loss of treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for damages caused; possible disqualification from directorships and travel restrictions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to report cross-border transactions or comply with beneficial ownership registers
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to 1 million EUR or 5% of turnover, criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment for willful non-compliance, and director disqualification
